title: Two libraries, one report
description:
The starter contains two small libraries, each documented only by the comments in its code: `minicsv`, which reads CSV records, and `minitpl`, which fills in text templates. Without changing them, use them to build a report generator. Everything you need to know about how they behave, including how they report errors, is in their comments: read them as you would a reference page.

```cpp-norun
std::optional<std::string> report(std::string_view csv, std::string_view rowTemplate, std::string& error);
```

**report** turns each data row of a CSV table into one line of text:

1. The **first record** of the CSV is the header: the column names.
2. For every following record (data rows numbered 1, 2, 3 ...), make a set of variables: each column name with that row's value, plus `row`, the row's number, unless a column is already called `row`. Render `rowTemplate` with them and add the result and a `\n` to the report.
3. Return the whole report and set `error` to an empty string. A table with a header and no data rows gives an empty report.

On the first problem, stop, return an empty optional, and set `error`:

| Problem | `error` |
|---|---|
| the CSV has no records at all | `no header` |
| a record has a different number of fields from the header | `csv line N: expected K fields` |
| the CSV reader reports an error | `csv line N: ` followed by the reader's error text |
| rendering a row fails | `row R: ` followed by the template's error text |

`N` is the line on which the problem record **starts** (the reader can tell you), `K` the number of header fields and `R` the data row number.
hints: The reader's `next` returns false for two different reasons. After your loop ends, `error()` tells you which: empty means the normal end of the text.
`minitpl::render` reports its error through the pointer you pass. Pass the address of a local string, and use it only when the result is empty.

Take the line number for a message from `reader.line()` right after the `next` call that read (or failed to read) the problem record: it is the line where that record started, even when the record spans several lines.
requirements: Uses the two libraries only through their documented functions, unchanged.
Builds one line per data row with the right variables, including `row` and the rule for a column called `row`.
Reports each problem with the exact message, line or row number, and stops at the first.
Handles quoted fields, blank lines and Windows line endings the way the CSV library documents.
